thread:
maria: Heads-up - aegis9b-int4 canary started showing two issues after yesterday's quant rollout: 1) sporadic OOMs on long generations (>700 tokens) and 2) a small but consistent drop in answer-fidelity on our QA evals (~3% EM drop). Seen across 4 canary instances.
sam: can you paste a representative error/log and the canary config?
maria: log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-21T10:02:11Z] RuntimeError: CUDA OOM when allocating KV cache (wanted 1.1GB)
node=canary-ml-12 gpu0_free=3.8G total_gpu=24G pid=4821
route=/api/v1/generate/aegis9b-int4
cfg: quant=bits=4, backend=q4_legacy, prefetch=true, max_new_tokens_default=1024, batch_size=6
```
jia: int4 q4_legacy backend packs differently; tile alignment + allocator churn can cause frag and larger per-token footprint. Also the fidelity drop smells like quantization aliasing on MLP layers. Two tracks: immed mitigation for stability, and parallel quality rollback/hardening.
devin: propose immediate canary config changes: reduce defaults and add rejection guard. Suggested patch: 
```
quant:
  backend: q4_opt (try q4_gptq if available)
runtime:
  max_new_tokens_default: 256
  max_new_tokens_hard_limit: 512
  prefetch: false
  batch_size: 3
  kernel_flags:
    use_sparse_kernels: false
    stable_alloc: true
memory:
  slot_compactor:
    enabled: true
    cadence: 5m
  kv_prune:
    enable: true
    min_age_seconds: 1200
```
sam: agree. Also suggest running a small A/B: keep two nodes on q4_legacy and two nodes on q4_opt with identical request mixes and run our QA regression suite (1000 short QA prompts + 200 long-form generations) to measure fidelity delta and mem profile.
maria: I'll apply the stability patch (max_new_tokens/ingress guard + prefetch off) now and stand up the A/B experiment. Adding a middleware guard to reject client requests with max_tokens>512 (429 + message).
ops-bot: Deployment event: canary "aegis9b-int4-canary-20260321-2" applied - prefetch=false, max_new_tokens_default=256, batch_size=3, ingress-guard=max_tokens<=512
jia: for the quality side can we run a re-quant compile using q4_gptq and a per-layer calibrator on the MLP layers? Sometimes a per-channel fine-tune (PTQ+bias corr) fixes the ~3% EM loss without needing int8.
devin: yes. workflow: 1) run q4_gptq offline with 512 calibration samples, 2) compare logits-perplexity and exact-match on our eval set, 3) if q4_gptq still bad, fallback to per-layer int8 for MLPs while keeping attention in int4.
maria: kicked off A/B perf+qa run. Baseline (pre-patch) had 0.9 OOMs/hr across pool; after patch initial 20m shows 0 OOMs and GPU headroom +2.6GB on affected nodes.
sam: perfect. keep an eye on latency and throughput impact from batch_size=3. If tail latency spikes >25% we may need to re-tune batching policy instead of hard lowering batch_size (e.g., adaptive microbatching).\ia: (typo)
jia: also adding a telemetry metric: per-token-kv-bytes labelled by quant backend so we have hard numbers comparing q4_legacy vs q4_gptq vs int8. That'll help capacity planning.
maria: A/B early results (1h): q4_opt nodes: 0 OOMs, EM drop reduced to ~0.8% vs baseline; q4_legacy nodes: still intermittent OOMs under long-form and EM drop ~3.1%. Per-token KV: q4_legacy ~210 bytes/token, q4_opt ~178 bytes/token, int8 ~160 bytes/token.
devin: based on that, plan: 1) promote q4_opt compile across canary pool, 2) run integration regen checks, 3) schedule a controlled ramp to 25% over next 12h with autoscale off. Also open a follow-up to evaluate hybrid quant (attn=int4, mlp=int8) for final rollout if needed.
sam: sounds good. i'll draft the rollout playbook and add rollback criteria: >1 OOM/hr or EM regression >1.5% sustained for 30m.
maria: promoting q4_opt now. Deploy-bot: Promotion event: aegis9b-int4-quant-switch -> q4_opt applied to canary pool.
ops-bot: Smoke test summary: 1000 QA queries run: q4_opt EM delta vs fp16 = -0.9%, latency p95 +12%, throughput -10%. No OOMs.
jia: acceptable for now, keep monitoring quality regressions alerts and add eval hooks to nightly canary runs.
maria: closing thread for now. Will file a short postmortem with the per-token KV numbers and quant compile config. Follow-ups: hybrid-quant experiment, telemetry dashboard for per-token-kv, and update default max_new_tokens for long-form routes.
